sections.h1: Custody and trading fail in public, and once
lead: A wallet that loses keys or an exchange that mis-settles a trade does not get a second launch. The architecture has to be right before any customer value moves through it.

p: Custodial and non-custodial wallets for web and mobile, with key management designed around who can sign what.
Hot and cold storage separation, approval workflows, and recovery procedures that are written down and tested.
Order books, matching and settlement engines, and the admin and reporting tools around them.
Integration with payment gateways and banking rails so users can move between fiat and digital assets.
Threat modelling and code review before launch, and independent audit where the risk justifies it.
EVM chains and others as the product needs. We choose per use case rather than by habit.
Agree what is held, who can move it and what the worst credible failure looks like.
Design key handling, settlement flow and failure modes before any feature work.
Develop in small releases, each with tests against the failure modes already listed.
Internal review and, where appropriate, external audit before real value is at stake.
Staged release with limits, monitoring and a rehearsed incident procedure.
Licensing and compliance for custody or trading depend on the jurisdiction and are your responsibility to settle with counsel and the regulator. We build to the requirements you confirm.

cards.h: Custom software, including wallets and gateways

faq.q: Do you build custodial or non-custodial wallets?
a: Either. The choice depends on who should hold the keys, what regulation applies and how users expect to recover access.

faq.q: Can you build a full exchange?
a: We build the trading, matching and settlement components and the tooling around them. Licensing and market operations remain with you.

faq.q: Do you audit your own contracts?
a: We review our own work internally. For higher-value systems we recommend an independent audit as well.

faq.q: Which blockchains do you work with?
a: We work across EVM-compatible chains and others where the product needs them. The choice is made per project.
